introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Duration: 1 hour 45 minutes.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
This question is based on the passage below:

> The existence of internal economies of scale provides a major force encouraging firms to grow in size. However there are different ways in which firms can grow. Broadly these can be classified as internal growth or external growth. When firms grow by amalgamation, there is a mutual agreement between them and in this case it is called merger. Growth can also occur when <u>one firm acquires control of another firm by obtaining at least 51% of its equity</u>.

*Source: Adapted from Introductory Economics by Barry Harrison. Page 70*

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following as used in the passage:

(i) Internal economies of scale. (2 marks)

(ii) Equity. (2 marks)

(iii) Merger. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Internal economies of scale.** These are the reductions in a firm's **average (unit) cost** of production that arise from the growth of the firm's *own* scale of output, because of factors inside the firm (larger plant, specialised labour, bulk buying, etc.), as opposed to external economies that come from the growth of the whole industry.

**(ii) Equity.** Equity is the **ownership capital of a company**, that is, the share capital (ordinary shares) held by shareholders. Holding a given percentage of a firm's equity means owning that percentage of its voting shares, so holding at least 51% gives control of the firm.

**(iii) Merger.** A merger (amalgamation) is the **joining together of two or more firms into one new or enlarged firm by mutual agreement** of their owners, usually through an exchange of shares, so that the separate firms cease to exist independently.

questions.enonce_markdown: List four internal economies of scale. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four internal economies of scale (any four; one mark each):

1. **Technical economies** - large firms can use large, efficient machines and mass-production methods whose cost per unit falls as output rises (indivisibilities), and they can divide labour into specialised tasks.
2. **Managerial economies** - a large firm can afford specialist managers (finance, marketing, production), so decisions are better and the cost of management per unit of output falls.
3. **Financial economies** - large firms are considered less risky, so they borrow more easily and at lower interest rates and can raise capital by issuing shares.
4. **Marketing (and purchasing) economies** - bulk buying of raw materials earns trade discounts, and the cost of advertising and distribution is spread over a larger output.
5. **Risk-bearing economies** - a large firm can diversify its products and markets so that a fall in demand for one product is offset by others.

Research and development economies and welfare economies are other acceptable examples.

questions.enonce_markdown: What economic term can be used to describe the underlined phrase? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: The underlined phrase, "one firm acquires control of another firm by obtaining at least 51% of its equity", describes a **takeover** (also called an **acquisition**). The acquiring firm buys a controlling (majority) holding of the shares of the other firm, which therefore passes under its control. Unlike a merger, it does not require a mutual agreement between the two firms: it can be friendly or hostile.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two ways by which a firm can grow internally. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Internal (organic) growth is growth that comes from the firm's own resources, without taking over another firm. Two ways (any two; 2 marks each with a short explanation):

1. **Ploughing back profits (retained earnings)** - the firm uses part of its undistributed profit to buy more machinery, build new factories or open new branches, which raises its productive capacity.
2. **Increasing sales through product development and marketing** - the firm introduces new products, improves quality and advertises more strongly, so that its market share and output increase.

Other acceptable ways: raising new capital by issuing new shares or by borrowing to finance expansion, and opening new outlets or entering new regional markets (for example, a Douala firm opening branches in other towns).

questions.enonce_markdown: Name two types of mergers. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two types of merger (2 marks each, with a brief description):

1. **Horizontal merger** - firms at the *same stage* of production in the *same industry* combine (for example, two breweries). It increases market share and allows economies of scale, but it reduces competition.
2. **Vertical merger** - firms at *different stages* of production of the same good combine. It can be a *backward* vertical merger (towards the source of raw materials, for example a chocolate maker joining a cocoa producer) or a *forward* vertical merger (towards the consumer, for example a manufacturer joining a retailer). It secures supplies or outlets.

A third type is the **conglomerate merger**, which joins firms in unrelated industries to spread risk (diversification).
